thread:
maya: Quick sync — we need to reconcile how client identity is propagated from edge to the fairness scheduler so abuse signals are accurate. Two high-level options: 1) full identity (signed id token) through the infra, 2) anonymized fingerprinting with score + TTL. Thoughts?
aj: Option 1 gives best auditorability but increases PII scope. Any KMS/KYC concerns?
sam: +1 on auditorability for debugging abuse incidents. But option 1 sounds heavy for low-trust clients. We should probably hybrid: tenant-id + ephemeral client-hash.
lena: Hybrid makes sense. Tenant-level quotas + per-client smoothing via ephemeral hashes. We need to define fingerprint rotation policy though.
maya: Agreed. From the fairness scheduler POV we need something stable across a short window (minutes) so batching/x-scheduling works. Ephemeral hash should be stable for ~5m by default.
carla: Also consider bots and SDK clients that will have consistent TLS certs — those should get a different signal. We can tag `client_type` in the token header.
aj: Implementation nit: propose edge emits header `X-RI-Client` that contains `tenant:<id>|hash:<h>|type:<sdk|web|bot>` and is HMAC-signed by edge with key version. Router verifies HMAC and passes through.
sam: HMACing avoids exposing raw IDs to downstream, nice. But we must ensure the fairness scheduler can trust HMAC provenance. That implies shared key/attestation between edge and scheduler. Are we comfortable with key sync?
lena: We can use token signing service (existing KMS-backed signing) and include `sig_v:<n>` in header. Scheduler verifies via public key lookup. No secret sync.
maya: That solves trust. How about quota semantics: tenant quotas remain absolute, per-client smoothing is soft (probabilistic delay or penalty). We should avoid hard blocking on hash mismatch unless extreme.
carla: For abuse detection we also want rate-derivative features (burstiness over 1m/5m/1h). The edge should emit a lightweight telemetry envelope for those metrics, sampled 1%.
aj: Telemetry sampling: 1% might miss spikes from smaller tenants. Maybe sample by tenant: for tenants > X qps sample differently. Or use deterministic sampling (hash mod N).
sam: Deterministic sampling based on client hash is good — gives us consistent traces for anomaly hunting.
lena: Rollout plan: (a) implement `X-RI-Client` header at edge (opt-in), (b) add verifier in router, (c) extend fairness scheduler to consume `client_hash` + `client_type` and apply smoothing window, (d) enable telemetry sampling. Start in canary region with a few tenants.
maya: Ops concerns: need migration playbook for keys, and a fallback when signature verification fails (allow but mark `sig=fail` so scheduler treats as untrusted).
carla: Also add privacy note in docs: hashed client IDs are not reversible, rotation policy, retention TTL 7 days by default.
aj: Security check: ensure HMAC keys rotate and revocation propagates. Add `sig_v` and `sig_exp` fields to header.
maya: Action items: @aj prototype header & signer (due EOW), @sam add verifier in router (next week), @lena schema + scheduler changes (two-week spike), @carla telemetry sampling draft (3 days). I'll schedule a follow-up on Thursday.
deploy-bot: Canary flag `client-identity-hdr` toggled ON for region-us-west at 1781234350 :rocket:
aj: Quick Q: do we want the router to strip original IP from downstream when header present? Privacy/compliance might require it.
lena: I think we should keep IP for internal security signals but not persist it long-term. Mask before storing long-term logs.
maya: Good. Anyone object to the hybrid approach? No objections -> move forward. :thumbsup:
carla: I'll draft the RFC follow-up with header schema + examples. Will include the sample header and verification pseudo-code:```
X-RI-Client: tenant:acme|hash:3f9a2c|type:sdk|sig_v:2|sig:BASE64
// verifier: verify(pubkey[v], tenant + '|' + hash + '|' + type, sig)
```
sam: FYI, need to update the canary dashboards to show `client_hash` cardinality so we can spot overfitting.
maya: Thanks everyone. Follow-up doc link will be posted in this thread.
